name: Michael T. Tolley
title: Professor
fitReason: Recent tactile policy work creates a genuine robot-learning overlap with a lab otherwise centered on soft hardware and design. A bounded sensor-policy comparison could suit a CS researcher, subject to an independently approved visit.

physicalEvidence.summary: TacO (May 21, 2026) trains and executes ACT visuomotor policies on physical Franka Panda arms at two institutions, comparing six tactile sensors across mass-uncertain pick-and-place, plug insertion and reorientation. Tolley is a coauthor and current coadvised postdoc Myungsun Park participates. The paper does not assign each apparatus to a particular PI, so physical access is treated as collaborative rather than guaranteed in Tolley’s own laboratory.

shortVisit.summary: The live Opportunities page describes degree admission, research for current UCSD master’s students and undergraduate work longer than one quarter. It contains no verified external-master’s short-visit instruction. Past visiting graduate students on the People page are precedent only; no opportunity points.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct tactile imitation-learning overlap, within a predominantly soft-design laboratory.
scoreReasons.physical: Current real-robot coauthored experiments and supervised-postdoc participation; precise PI apparatus ownership unresolved.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: External-master’s visit unknown; local MS instructions and past visitors do not establish a current route.

unknowns: The current UCSD Profiles and lab People pages say Professor; the Materials Science programme page still says Associate Professor. Current rank follows the two consistent primary sources.
ACT is an imitation-learning transformer, not a diffusion policy. Tactile input is not universally helpful: improvements vary with task and sensor.

The coadvised-postdoc connection supports attributable current participation, but the exact individual laboratory hardware allocation is unresolved. Former postdoc Yi Sha is listed as an alumnus in the live university-domain page, despite an older Google Sites mirror retaining him among current members.

Existing UCSD institutional review explicitly supports non-UC visiting graduate students, including master’s, with no minimum appointment duration and possible personal funding. Host, department, graduate division and immigration approval remain necessary; this is not lab acceptance.

Summer 2027 acceptance, mentor capacity, exact dates, funding, visitor appointment, and applicable university/immigration approvals remain unconfirmed. Self-funding alone does not establish eligibility.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
